We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps enumerated in order they must be applied (forward). Steps: 1) Carboxylic acid to amide via coupling (amide formation). 2) Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (C=C). 3) Sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give carboxylic acid and aniline (or amine). Then break the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid to aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid. So retrosynthesis: the unsaturated acid fragment (the side chain attached to sulfonyl phenyl) can be disconnected to aromatic aldehyde (p-? ) and malonic acid (or its derivative). The sulfonamide formation forward: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the other phenyl with methyl). So overall route:

Step 1 (retro): break sulfonamide bond: produce aryl sulfonyl chloride (p-chlorobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Actually target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl ring (c2...). The sulfonyl chloride precursor would be p-chlorobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl part is attached to phenyl ring with the unsaturated side chain. The sulfonyl chloride would be that phenyl sulfonyl chloride (i.e., 4-(... )-chlorosulfonyl? Actually the sulfonyl chloride would be the phenyl ring bearing the side chain as a substituent? In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) and the sulfonyl is attached to the aniline (the other phenyl). So sulfonyl chloride precursor: 4-(α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid phenyl) sulfonyl chloride (i.e., 4-(E)-3-(carboxy)styryl phenyl sulfonyl chloride). That seems plausible.

Step 2 (retro): break the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid to aldehyde (the phenyl aldehyde) and malonic acid (or its derivative). The aldehyde would be 4-(E)-styryl? Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N... The unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl via double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-COOH. So the aldehyde precursor would be phenyl-CHO (p-formyl phenyl) with the same substitution pattern (the phenyl bearing the sulfonyl). So the aldehyde is 4-formyl phenyl attached to sulfonyl? Wait the sulfonyl is attached to that phenyl, not the aldehyde. The unsaturated acid is attached to the phenyl that also has the sulfonyl group. So the aldehyde would be that phenyl with sulfonyl group? Actually the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via nitrogen (sulfonamide). In the unsaturated acid fragment, the sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl ring, not to the aldehyde carbon. So the aldehyde precursor would be the same phenyl ring bearing sulfonyl chloride? No, the sulfonyl is attached to the other phenyl (the methyl phenyl). Let's parse target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have two phenyl rings: ring A: methyl phenyl (para-methyl). It has NSO2 attached to it (sulfonamide). The sulfonyl group attaches to ring B: phenyl with side chain /C=C/C(=O)N... So ring B is attached to sulfonyl via S=O2 to the phenyl (i.e., sulfonyl attached to ring B). So sulfonamide formation: aniline (ring A with NH2) reacts with sulfonyl chloride derived from ring B (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So retro step 1: break N-S bond to give aniline (ring A with NH2) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (ring B with sulfonyl chloride). Good.

Step 2: The aryl sulfonyl chloride contains the side chain /C=C/C(=O)N... Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to ring B at the sulfonyl group, and ring B also has the side chain (α,β-unsaturated amide). In forward, after sulfonamide formation, the side chain is already present. So retro step 2: break the amide bond (C=O attached to N-aryl) to give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). That's the amide formation step. So we need to disconnect the amide to give the unsaturated acid and aniline (aniline is the aniline attached to the amide). So the unsaturated acid is phenyl-CH=CH-COOH (attached to ring B). So retro step 2 yields that acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Good.

Step 3: The unsaturated acid is formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (the same phenyl ring B with aldehyde) and malonic acid. So retro step 3: break the C=C and COOH to give aldehyde (phenyl-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So we have three steps.

Thus we need to propose route with three reactions, each with template IDs. We need to find appropriate template IDs for each transformation.

We have template search results earlier: For sulfonamide formation, we saw template ID 1313644 (reaction_id) with retro_smarts that seems to be sulfonamide formation (Cl-[S...]-[c] + [NH2] -> sulfonamide). That template likely works for our case. Template ID is reaction_id? The tool returns reaction_id and template_hash. The template ID to use in apply_template etc is likely the reaction_id? The spec says template_id is identifier of retrosynthetic template. Probably reaction_id works. We'll use 1313644.

For amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide), we need a template. Search for amide formation. Let's search for functional groups broken: amide, formed: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines. We attempted earlier and got empty. Maybe need to search for amide formed? Actually forward reaction is amide formation, so retro we break amide to acid + amine. So functional_groups_broken: amide, formed: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines. That gave empty. Maybe need to use "carboxylic esters" etc. Let's search for templates where amide is formed (i.e., forward amide formation). Could search for functional_groups_formed: amide, broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines.
